Method of Attack: Monitors Windows event logs for application crashes and shows a popup with an alarming message to trick users into calling a tech support scam phone number
Distributed as a secondary payload in bundled software installs
Installs a scheduled task (RunAtStartup) that executes em.exe
em.exe connects to a remote server to download configuration files with localized scam phone numbers and scam messages
Popup uses localized phone numbers targeting users in US, Germany, France, Japan
Popup appears only after legitimate app crashes to convince users their PC is at risk
Indicators of Compromise: Files in %UserProfile%\AppData\Roaming\Event Monitor\ including em.exe, update.ini, localized INI files
Windows scheduled task named RunAtStartup located at C:\Windows\System32\Tasks\RunAtStartup
Registry entries under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Event Monitor and HKCU\Software\Event Monitor
Phone numbers used in scam popups: (844) 763-5838 (US), 01.76.54.05.61 (France), (800) 180-6512 (Germany), 03-5050-1410 (Japan)
